steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add lasagna and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente. Rinse in cold water and drain well.

Meanwhile, in a large sauce pan over medium heat add oil and cook broccoli or spinach and green onions until tender, stirring frequently. Remove pan from heat and stir in ricotta cheese, Parmesan cheese, salt and egg.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Place noodles in a single layer on a sheet of waxed paper. Evenly spread some of the cheese mixture on each noodle. Roll up each noodle from the short end, jelly-roll style.

In a 8x12 inch baking dish, spoon about 3/4 of the Alfredo sauce on the bottom and spread evenly. Arrange the rolled noodles, seam side down, in the dish. Top with mozzarella cheese and remaining sauce. Cover loosely with foil and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly and the cheese is melted. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Lasagna Alfredo Roll Ups
raw_recipe.description: Impress dinner guests with these picture-perfect portions of lasagna. Roll up cooked noodles with a spinach/ricotta filling and bake with a blanket of creamy rich Alfredo sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was definitely a wonderful dish. I made a few changes with great results: I made 10 instead of 8, otherwise the spinach mixture would have been too much in each. I also added sauteed mushrooms (1/2 pkg) and 2 finely chopped chicken breasts. I poured roasted red pepper pasta sauce on the bottom of the pan and a little over each one before ladling on the alfredo. This way, it was a little lighter, the sauces complemented each other... and it all looked nice too. Try it, you'll like it!

This is a very delicious, rich lasagna. I made an alfredo sauce (Chef John's light version with garlic) and it was very flavourful. Added cooked chicken for more protein. Squeezed most of the water out of the frozen greens before adding the cheese and used onion powder. Appreciated the recommendation to dry the noodles before adding the filling - worked great! Cooked it 30 minutes then removed cover to brown for 15 min. This would be nice to make when entertaining friends (nice salad and wine).

This is one of the best recipes I’ve ever made. I used homemade Alfredo sauce and added three mild Italian sausages to the spinach and ricotta mixture. These were absolutely delicious and based on other recommendations, use 10 lasagna sheets instead of 8 and make sure they are dry before you start to spread the mixture. Will definitely make these again!

Delicious recipe. My husband loved it. I did what some of the other reviewers suggested and added shredded chicken to the filling and spread tomato basil sauce on the bottom of the casserole dish and poured the rest on top of the lasagna rolls followed by the Alfredo sauce. Perfect with a salad.

This was good and I will definitely make it again. I made a few changes.. I followed other reviews and added some tomato sauce at the bottom of the dish. I also used fresh spinach, broccoli, and garlic and sautéed it in olive oil. I made my own Alfredo. 2-3 rolls per person

Sooo delicious! My family loved it! Followed the recipe and only modified it as follows: used 9 lasagne noodles, whole milk ricotta, 1/3 cup Parmesan, 1 jar Alfredo-pesto sauce (made the flavor pop!) and 1/2 jar marinara sauce for the bottom of the dish. Thanks for an awesome recipe!

I used fresh spinach (bad childhood memories of the frozen stuff) and added 3 cloves of garlic. Couldn't find an organic Alfredo so I went with emril's roasted garlic Alfredo in a pinch. After one bite my husband said I can definitely make it again. I rarely hear that from him so it was a hit! Cooked at 375 for about 40 mins - recipe didn't specify which really threw off an inexperienced cook like me.

This was super yummy! I used the Four Cheese Alfredo sauce from Aldi, and it was really good. It was only 15 oz, and it was the perfect amount. I sauteed five cloves of garlic with some red pepper flakes and added it to the spinach. I didn't have any green onions, so I just added some onion powder to the ricotta cheese. Great recipe!

This was a great hit with my family and guests. It looks very elegant and tastes very yummy. I made a few changes suggested in earlier comments. I used a bottled red sauce on the bottom to lighten the richness of the dish. I added some shredded rotisserie chicken which was good, but not really necessary . I used fresh mozzarella instead of the dryer store bought shredded mozzarella and added it into the filling as well as in top of the rolls. This made the bottom sauce of the cooked dish a little watery because of the extra moisture in the fresh mozzarella. Next time I will either use less mozzarella or switch to the shredded firmer mozzarella . I also made my own Alfredo sauce rather than bottled sauce. It was amazing but took a lot of time to reduce the heavy cream without using a thickener like flour. I will definitely make this again and just adjust some of my choices to keep this a quick and easy recipe as intended. This dish was rick a cheesy and enjoyed by both young and not so young. I served it with hot homemade French bread , balsamic green beans, green salad and fresh fruit. I can see many ways to adjust this recipe to make new recipes with different sauces and fillings. Much easier than traditional lasagna. Thank you for sharing this recipe. It will be a new addition to my definitely to be repeated list!

This is a wonderful way to enjoy lasagna and use up leftover uncooked lasagna noodles. I enjoy vegetables so I used 10 ounces of fresh spinach and portobello mushrooms and a palmful of sun dried tomatoes and sautéed until mushrooms were cooked and spinach wilted. After letting it cool for a bit then went on adding cheese and all as in the recipe. I always prefer the way the flavors blend and lasagna melds when having it the 2nd day.

awesome! i did change it up though. i cooked italian sausage, vodka sauce, onions, minced garlic, and itailian seasoning, lined the bottom of the pan with the mixture, then followed the rest of the recipe exactly. loved it!
I made it just as the recipe said we lived it

Very good dish. In particular, I liked the green onion. However, I did not cook the green onion. I used frozen spinach squeezed dry, so no need to saute it either. Solid and simple recipe. It was on the table in an hour (and I went very leisurely). Finally, the recipe was light on spices and herbs, so I added dried parsley and dried Italian seasoning Solid recipe. It is going in my saved file.
I made a half recipe (4 servings) since it was just me - it was delicious, and I'll make it again. I'm freezing half (2 servings), hopefully it freezes well.

So....I really liked the flavors of this one, that was the strongest point. My challenge was the consistency of the filling. Mine was too thin to put a good amount in the noodle to roll. I ended up switching to the traditional lasagna layer method. In the future, I may attempt to make the rollups using a muffin tin instead.
What a great alternate way to use lasagna! This dish was super tasty. I added a little minced garlic and topped it with olives because my wife and I are big fans. But this dish needed no improvement!

Very nice quick delicious tasting recipe. I added seasoned shredded chicken, fresh garlic and broccoli with a few spoons of mozzarella cheese to the filling no eggs. After cooking 30 minutes, I let it brown for 10 minutes to get a beautiful color. Will definitely make this again.
Was looking for something flavorful and moist for mother with cancer. She hasn't been able to eat much but she couldn't get enough of this amazing dish. Thank you for posting.
